([[Northfield, Massachusetts]]) | college = * [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]] (2018–2019) * [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] (2020–2021) | highlights = }} '''Dalano Banton''' (born November 7, 1999) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]] and the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Banton, originally a member of 2019 class, reclassified into 2018. He played for Redemption Christian Academy in [[Northfield, Massachusetts]] and [[MacDuffie School]] in [[Granby, Massachusetts]].{{cite news |last1=Stephens |first1=Brad |title= Hilltoppers sign 4-Star Canada native Dalano Banton |url= https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/hilltoppers-sign-4-star-canada-native-dalano-banton/article_f60a04cb-022c-5b40-a4b5-c76d202cd21b.html |accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=[[Bowling Green Daily News]] |date=November 14, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== By the end of his high school career, Banton was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was ranked in the top 100 recruits nationally in 2018 by Rivals (No. 80) and 247Sports (No. 92). On November 14, 2017, Banton chose [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]] over [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]], and [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].{{cite news |last1=Stephens |first1=Brad |title= Hilltoppers sign 4-Star Canada native Dalano Banton |url= https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/hilltoppers-sign-4-star-canada-native-dalano-banton/article_f60a04cb-022c-5b40-a4b5-c76d202cd21b.html |accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=[[Bowling Green Daily News]] |date=November 14, 2017}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Dalano Banton | position = [[Point guard|PG]] / [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Toronto, Ontario|Toronto, ON]] | highschool = Redemption Christian Academy (MA) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 185 | 40 = | commitdate = November 14, 2017 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 0 | espn grade = NR }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Western Kentucky 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers Recruiting Class | rivals school = westernkentucky | scout s = | espn schoolid = 98 | 247 overall = 92 | rivals overall = 80 | espn overall = | accessdate = January 1, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== As a freshman, Banton played 31 games at Western Kentucky, averaging 3.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game. Banton made 12 starts and nearly had a triple-double with 13 rebounds, 10 assists and eight points in a career-high 38 minutes in a win over No. 15 [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{cite web |title=Dalano Banton Helps Western Kentucky Beat No. 15 Wisconsin 83-76|url= https://www.si.com/college/2018/12/30/dalano-banton-western-kentucky-wisconsin |access-date=January 1, 2021 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=December 29, 2018}} Banton was one of only six players in Division I basketball to have a game with at least eight points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists in 2018–19. He had three double-figure scoring efforts on the season, including a season-high 11 points against both [[Belmont Bruins men's basketball|Belmont]] and [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]], as he also had six assists and three blocks against the Gaels.{{cite web |title=Dalano Banton WKU Bio |url= https://wkusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dalano-banton/1682 |access-date=January 1, 2021 |work=WKU Sports |date=March 25, 2019}} On April 10, 2019, Banton announced his intent to transfer from Western Kentucky.{{cite news |last1=Shircliffe |first1=Ross |title= WKU Basketball: Dalano Banton to Transfer From Hill |url= https://medium.com/the-red-towel/wku-basketball-report-dalano-banton-to-transfer-from-hill-30345f720d06 |accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=WKU Herald Sports |date=April 10, 2019}} On May 1, 2019, Banton announced, via Twitter, his commitment to Nebraska.{{cite news |last1=Basnett |first1=Chris |title= Huskers get commitment from 6-foot-8 transfer guard Banton |url= https://journalstar.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/huskers-get-commitment-from-6-foot-8-transfer-guard-banton/article_c8038433-cca5-554c-8c74-823594711d0a.html |accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=[[Lincoln Journal Star]] |date=May 1, 2019}} Banton sat out the 2019–20 season after transferring from Western Kentucky and honed his skills on the scout team. Banton played during the Huskers' trip to Italy in August of 2019, averaging 5.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists, and 1.3 steals per game in helping the Huskers post a 4–0 record.{{cite web |title=Dalano Banton Nebraska Bio |url= https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dalano-banton/42007 |access-date=January 1, 2021 |work=Huskers.com |date=September 1, 2020}} On December 17, 2020, Banton recorded just the second triple-double in Nebraska men’s basketball history with 13 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in Nebraska's 110–64 win over [[Doane University]].{{cite news |last1=Ward|first1=Andrew|title= Banton records triple double, Husker Hoops routes Doane |url= https://www.klkntv.com/banton-records-triple-double-husker-hoops-routes-doane/|accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=[[KLKN]] |date=December 17, 2020}} He averaged 9.6 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=DuBose |first1=Ben |title=Report: Nebraska prospect Dalano Banton to work out with Rockets |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2021/06/16/report-nebraska-prospect-dalano-banton-to-work-out-with-rockets/ |access-date=June 25, 2021 |work=Rockets Wire |date=June 16, 2021}} However, on July 2 he announced he was remaining in the draft.{{cite news |title=Dalano Banton Stays in 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://huskers.com/news/2021/7/2/mens-basketball-dalano-banton-stays-in-2021-nba-draft.aspx |access-date=July 4, 2021 |work=Husker Athletics |date=July 2, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]] | '''31''' || 12 || 15.1 || .402 || .216 || .559 || 3.0 || 2.1 || .5 || .5 || 3.4 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] | style="text-align:center;" colspan="11"|
